% 01.12.2025 1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.

2. Application stands disposed of.
CRL.REV.P.(MAT.) 523/2025 3.

The present revision petition has been filed by the petitioners under Section 442 of BNSS, 2023 against the impugned judgment/order dated 15.10.2025 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-04/North-East District, Karkardooma Court, Delhi in CRL.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-04/North-East District, Karkardooma Court, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: APPL. No. 149/2025, whereby the appeal filed by present petitioners was dismissed on the ground of delay.

4. The said appeal was preferred by the petitioners against the order dated 22.06.2024 passed by the learned Trial Court-02, North-East District, Karkardooma Court, Delhi, whereby petitioners were directed to jointly pay the compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- to the respondent Smt. Anjum.

entities.text: Trial Court-02, North-East District, Karkardooma Court, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

Learned counsel for petitioners submits that delay was explained by the petitioners.

Elaborating further, he submits that appeal could not be preferred within time as petitioners were not aware of the proceedings, however, learned Trial Court did not appreciate this contention of petitioners in proper perspective.

sentences.text: He contends that the contention of petitioners was rejected on the ground that there was another case FIR bearing no. 258/2022 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at PS-Dayal Pur, which was pending before the same Trial Court.

7. He contends that the fact recorded by the learned Appellate Court is factually incorrect, inasmuch as the impugned order was passed on 22.06.2024, whereas the chargesheet in connection with FIR No. 258/2022 was filed by the police only on 16.07.2024, in which summons were for 14.09.2024.
8.

He further contends that in the meanwhile the learned Trial Court in execution proceedings had attached the vehicle of the petitioner no. 1, who is father of the husband of respondent no.2.
9.
He submits that vehicle is a car, which was being used by petitioner no.1 for earning his livelihood.
10. In view of the above, issue notice.
11. Ms. Richa Dhawan, learned APP for State accepts notice.

12. Let status report be filed before the next date of hearing indicating the status of vehicle that was seized vide seizure memo dated 13.10.2025 (Annexure-P6).
13.
On petitioner taking steps, issue notice to respondent no.2 by all permissible modes returnable on 15.12.2025.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 03/12/2025 at 21:36:40 14.
In the meanwhile, learned Executing Court is directed not to proceed with the auction of the vehicle.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J DECEMBER 1, 2025/

9.
He submits that vehicle is a car, which was being used by petitioner no.1 for earning his livelihood.
